column5: Purdue HO-237-W read in full: nutrients readily available at pH 5.4 to 6.2; alkalinity raises pH over time and irrigation water should be lab-tested first; three methods (PourThru, saturated media extract, 1:2 dilution) with the advantages, disadvantages, pot-size water table and EC interpretation table exactly as module 4 gives them; the crop groups are ornamentals only, as the course already notes.

Purdue HO-237-W procedure detail: for PourThru, water as usual, let the pot drain 30 to 60 minutes, then add distilled water to collect close to 50 mL (more than 70 mL dilutes); for saturated media extract, take 200 to 300 mL of substrate avoiding the top and bottom inch, wet to saturation with no free water, stand 30 minutes, then filter; for 1:2 dilution, mix one part substrate to two parts distilled water by volume and stand 30 minutes.

Purdue HO-237-W programme habits: take five to ten samples per crop type and average them; calibrate the meter with standards near the range tested (for example pH 4.0 for peat or bark); store meters and calibration solutions indoors at room temperature and low humidity, never in the greenhouse; have the same person test each time; graph the values, since the trend is the real value of testing.
